meta.title: External Orchestrators: Invisible to a Databricks-Only Inventory

views.label: It won't show up on its own
views.note: A job triggered from Airflow or ADF doesn't appear in a Databricks-only asset inventory scan.

views.label: Auth mechanism decides survival
views.note: Cloud-native identity federation from an orchestrator generally does not survive a cross-cloud move.

views.label: Run it, don't just connect it
views.note: A connectivity check proves the network path, not that the orchestrated pipeline actually still works.

cards.title: Easy to miss in discovery, on purpose
items: Airflow, ADF, Step Functions/Glue, and Cloud Composer jobs don't show up in a Databricks-only scan
Explicitly inventory every external scheduler with a Databricks connection before trusting the job inventory
Ask application teams directly — the platform team doesn't always know every trigger that exists

cards.title: The auth mechanism decides what survives
items: A PAT or OAuth service principal migrates cleanly to a target-scoped equivalent
Cloud-native identity federation — ADF's Entra ID auth, for example — has no equivalent if the target isn't that cloud
Hardcoded job/cluster IDs referenced directly in DAGs need updating after job recreation, not just the connection

cards.title: Run it end to end, not just connectivity
items: A network reachability check proves the path exists, not that the pipeline still works
Run each orchestrated pipeline against target before cutover, every time
Composer's VPC networking specifically needs to reach a private-only target endpoint if enforced
